MAE 2501 · Class C

Normal Force

Elevators and Space Shuttles
Practice Problem

What acceleration would an elevator need to make you feel 20% heavier? 20% lighter?

$$F_\text{N}=mg+m\ddot y\;\Rightarrow\; \ddot y=\left(\frac{F_\text{N}}{mg}-1\right)g$$

20% heavier: $F_\text{N}/mg=1.2 \rightarrow \ddot y=+0.2g\approx+2$ m/s² (up).
20% lighter: $F_\text{N}/mg=0.8 \rightarrow \ddot y=-0.2g\approx-2$ m/s² (down).

Practice Problems

Practice Problem

Suppose "Reindeer Games" lifts kids up and down in a sinusoidal motion, i.e. coaster height $y(t)=A\sin(2\pi f t)$. Taking $A=2$ m and $f=0.35$ Hz, what are the largest and smallest "g's" you experience, and where?

$$\ddot y=-A(2\pi f)^2\sin(2\pi f t),\qquad \frac{F_N}{mg}=1+\frac{\ddot y}{g}=1\pm\frac{A(2\pi f)^2}{g}$$

Heaviest at the bottom of the travel: $1+A(2\pi f)^2/g\approx 2g$. Lightest at the top: $1-A(2\pi f)^2/g\approx 0g$ — kids feel momentarily weightless.

Practice Problem

What if you designed a version of "Reindeer Games" that also moved kids at a constant horizontal speed $\dot{x}=4.4$ m/s while moving them up and down with the same vertical position ($y(t)=A\sin(2\pi f t)$ with $A=2$ m and $f=0.35$ Hz). Kids would then move along a sinusoidal track $y=A\sin(x\cdot 2\pi f / \dot{x})\approx 2\sin(0.5 x)$ (meters). What now would be the largest and smallest g's?

No acceleration in $x$, so same answer as before: $F_N/mg=1+\ddot y/g=$ 2$g$ at the troughs and $0g$ at the crests.
